full_effective_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: anatomical continuity reference for a fictional character, a healed old fingertip difference. Requested canvas 2304 x 1536, landscape.
Input image 1 is STYLE AND SKIN-AGE REFERENCE ONLY: approved Burtsev head sheet, not content to repeat. Do not draw his face, head or body. Draw only the one SAME LEFT hand repeated in three distinct nearby angles. Keep the rough matte expressive oil-brush paint, visible angular broken strokes, grey plain background and soft flat neutral studio light.

FULL CANONICAL CSV PROMPT_EN (preserve all):
Reference study sheet of one man's LEFT hand shown in three angles side by side: back of the hand toward the viewer, thumb and index finger pinching a wooden matchstick, middle, ring and little fingers loosely extended; the RING FINGER is missing its last joint: no fingernail, a smooth rounded healed stump, clearly shorter than the middle and little fingers; all other fingers complete with nails; weathered ruddy skin of a 54-year-old man, even neutral studio light, plain mid-grey background #6E7378, painterly oil study with visible brush strokes, no text, no labels

FULL CANONICAL CSV NEGATIVE_EN (avoid all):
intact ring finger, fingernail on the ring finger, six fingers, extra fingers, fused fingers, right hand, gloves, text

Precise anatomy and arrangement: Three isolated studies horizontally side by side at equal scale, with all digits clearly inside the canvas. This is a LEFT hand with the DORSAL BACK and nails facing us; in the first straight-on dorsal view the THUMB IS ON IMAGE-RIGHT. Reading the extended digits from image-left to image-right: LITTLE finger complete with nail; RING finger with only its distal/nail phalanx absent, two lower segments still present and a rounded fully healed skin end with NO NAIL; MIDDLE finger fully intact and longest; INDEX finger bent naturally toward the intact THUMB to pinch a single slender wooden matchstick. That is exactly FIVE digits per hand: thumb, index, middle, shortened ring, little. The shortened ring ends just below the little fingertip, and noticeably below the middle fingertip. Do not remove the entire ring finger, do not damage the little or middle fingers, do not draw an intact nail on the shortened ring. No gore, blood, open wound, fresh injury, stitches, bone or bandage. The intact index and thumb pinch the match at the right side of the hand; their natural bends do not turn them into extra fingers. The middle, ring and little remain loosely separated and extended so the exact ring difference is easy to inspect.
The second and third panels show the SAME LEFT hand with the SAME old healed ring-tip difference, same skin, same proportions and same match grip, turned modestly in two directions for dorsal-oblique study, not a mirrored right hand. Keep all five digits identifiable in each; do not rotate into full edge-on profile that hides the shortened ring. Lower forearm in a small worn brown leather cuff over dark knit sweater, matching the character reference, hand-focused crop. No frames, labels, words, numbers, arrows, diagrams, jewellery or props other than the match. Matte brushy paint, never photographic, smooth render or plastic.
